observations: Three photos show a used automotive AC compressor with a ribbed pulley, mounting brackets, and electrical connector.
The compressor is heavily soiled with grime and oil, with visible rust and wear on the metal casing.
No brand or model markings are visible on the compressor body in any photo.
The seller claims it is for a Ford F150 and 'Grade one' (implying good condition).
The watermark 'MICHAEL SOLAR GLOBAL' appears on all photos, suggesting a seller or reseller brand, not part of the item.

claims.evidence: No visual evidence of condition beyond surface grime and rust; 'Grade one' is subjective and not verifiable remotely.
No visible part numbers, VIN, or model-specific markings to confirm compatibility; seller's claim cannot be verified from photos alone.

risks.risk: Compressor may be non-functional or internally damaged
risks.proof: A video showing the compressor spinning freely and no internal noise when rotated by hand, or a test with power and refrigerant.

risks.risk: Incorrect fitment for Ford F150 (wrong model/year/engine)
risks.proof: Photo of the part number or VIN tag from the original vehicle or a clear shot of the compressor's casting number.

risks.risk: Severe internal wear or oil contamination
risks.proof: Close-up of the oil port or internal components if disassembled, or a test run with refrigerant.

proof_requests: Photo of the compressor's casting number or part number (if any) on the body.
Video of the compressor spinning freely by hand, with no grinding or binding.
Photo of the original vehicle's VIN or engine bay to confirm compatibility.
Photo of the electrical connector pins to match with the Ford F150's system.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as an AC compressor, but the seller's claims about grade and fitment cannot be verified from the photos. Critical risks like functionality and compatibility remain unproven, and without proof, pricing is not possible.
